standard.title: Arts importance for communities
standard.description: explore how and why the arts are important for people and communities
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior arts learning assumed. Students bring personal experience of music, song, stories and community celebrations from their family and cultural contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore how and why the arts are important for people and communities, and share their own observations and responses.

nodes.label: Arts in daily life
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify arts works and experiences in their own life and describe why they matter to them.
nodes.minimum_width: Name at least one arts experience from their daily life (e.g. a song they sing, a dance they know, a game with music) and say something about why it is meaningful or enjoyable.
nodes.typical_width: Identify arts works and experiences across multiple contexts — songs, dances, drama, animations, games, public art; share preferences and responses; connect personal arts experiences to what they mean for themselves and their family or community.
wider: Compile a class list of songs everyone knows — notice which songs are shared across the class and which are specific to certain families or cultures
Explore how music is used in celebrations the students know (birthday songs, school songs, sporting anthems) and compare their purposes

response_modes.reason: Students' awareness of arts in their lives varies enormously at Foundation. Broadening the contexts in which they notice arts (home, community, screen, ceremony) builds the experiential base for understanding why arts matter.

success_criteria: Can name at least one arts experience from their own life
Can describe why that experience is enjoyable or meaningful to them

nodes.label: How arts communicate emotions and ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe how an arts work (e.g. a song, a dance or a drawing) communicates an emotion or idea.
nodes.minimum_width: Observe one arts work (e.g. a song, a portrait, a dance) and identify one emotion or idea it communicates.
nodes.typical_width: Explore how facial expressions, gestures, voice and movement communicate emotions across different arts forms; listen to songs and discuss how the music makes them feel and why; explore how illustrations in picture books communicate mood and character.
wider: Compare how two different songs communicate the same emotion (e.g. joy) using different elements of music — what makes each feel joyful?
Explore how images in a picture book and the music in a song work together or differently to tell the same kind of story
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding that arts works communicate — that they are intentional acts of meaning-making — is the conceptual foundation for all exploring and responding work in subsequent years. Students who do not grasp this at Foundation approach arts engagement as passive entertainment rather than communication, which limits their capacity to analyse and respond to music in later bands.

response_modes.reason: Use guided questioning after listening or watching: 'How did that make you feel?', 'What do you think the singer/dancer/artist wanted to show?', 'How did they do that?' This builds the habit of reading arts works as communications, not just experiences.

success_criteria: Can identify one emotion or idea communicated by an arts work
Can describe (simply) one feature of the work that communicates that emotion or idea

nodes.label: Arts as important for communities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe at least one way that an arts work is important for a community — beyond personal enjoyment.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one way an arts work (e.g. a ceremony song, a school anthem, a community celebration) is important to a group of people, not just to themselves personally.
nodes.typical_width: Sing songs used for celebrations and discuss why they are used; explore how arts experiences are shared in their school community; listen to First Nations Australians talk about the importance of the arts for connecting to People, Culture and Country/Place.
wider: Investigate how a local cultural event (e.g. a school concert, a community festival) uses music — discuss what it does for the people who participate
Listen to First Nations Australians discuss the role of music and arts in connecting to Country/Place — compare this to how music is used in the students' own community

response_modes.reason: The concept that arts matter to communities (not just individuals) benefits from encountering multiple community contexts — school, family, cultural, ceremonial. Each new context adds evidence for why the arts have collective importance.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations Australian perspectives on arts and Country/Place offer a substantively different understanding of what arts do for communities — this is pedagogically significant and not covered by typical Western school-arts examples.
success_criteria: Can describe one way an arts work is important to a community (e.g. it brings people together, it celebrates something, it tells a story about who we are)
Can give at least one example from a community context beyond their own personal experience
